newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end slightly up on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end slightly up on bargain-hunting.

text.p: * Market awaits second quarter GNP figures
Bargain-hunting lifted Manila shares slightly on Wednesday after two days of losses, traders said.
The main index nudged up 4.59 points to 3,200.98 after Tuesday's 13.91-point fall.
"Investors have started to position since they expect good news," said trader Rudsend Alpay of Lippo Securities, referring to second quarter growth figures do for release next week.
Other analysts, however, think the market is only likely to take big strides after the GNP figures are released because it is currently trading at expensive levels.
"The market is still sideways. There is no reason to buy," said Spencer Yap, an analyst of BPI Securities, adding that investors would wait until the GNP figures are announced.
Yap estimated the market currently has an overall price-earnings ratio of 24 times 1996 forecast earnings.
Among the index stocks, Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co rose 10 pesos to 1,565 pesos.
